constraints: Do not modify any file under inputs/; submit only submission/recovered_key.json.
Do not assume access to a functional oracle beyond what yosys/iverilog/vvp simulation of the provided netlist itself can reveal; base structural claims on the netlist and locking_description.md.
The netlist is small enough (under 300 gate instances) to analyze by inspection or with yosys read_verilog + stat/show passes.
expected_outputs: submission/recovered_key.json listing per-key-bit findings (value or unknown), the wire names of all identified key-gating structures, and a topology summary of how those structures connect to the primary output(s)

functional_requirements.requirement: recovered_key.json must be valid JSON matching the pinned schema exactly: key_bits is a non-empty array covering every key input declared in locked_netlist.v (no duplicates, no missing bits), key_gate_locations is a non-empty array, and topology_summary is a non-empty string.

Every key_input name listed in key_bits and every gate/wire name listed in key_gate_locations must exactly match an identifier that actually exists in inputs/locked_netlist.v (verifiable by string search / yosys read).

For each key bit reported with value "0" or "1" (not "unknown"), confidence must be a number strictly greater than 0 and at most 1, and reasoning must be a non-empty string of at least 15 characters explaining the structural basis for the claim.
For any key bit reported as "unknown", confidence must be reported as 0.

interface: The submission is a single JSON file at submission/recovered_key.json (no other files are graded). Its top-level schema is: {"key_bits": [{"key_input": string (exact wire name from locked_netlist.v, e.g. "key[3]"), "value": "0"|"1"|"unknown", "confidence": number in [0,1], "reasoning": string}], "key_gate_locations": [string] (exact wire/gate instance names in locked_netlist.v that implement key-dependent gating logic), "topology_summary": string (free-text description of how the identified gating structure(s) connect between the locked internal net(s) and the primary output(s), including the names of the internal nets/output ports involved)}. evaluate.py parses this JSON, cross-references key_input names and key_gate_locations against inputs/locked_netlist.v, and may optionally invoke yosys/iverilog/vvp on locked_netlist.v to simulate reported key values and confirm claimed output behavior.
objective: You are given a gate-level combinational netlist (Verilog) that has been logic-locked using an unspecified key-insertion scheme, along with a short description of the locking methodology. The netlist contains a set of key inputs (named key[0], key[1], ... or KEY0, KEY1, ...) that must be set to the correct secret values for the circuit to compute its intended function; incorrect key values cause wrong outputs. Analyze the netlist structure and produce a report identifying: (1) which gates/wires form the key-gating logic, (2) how the key inputs feed into the circuit topology, and (3) any key bit values that can be determined purely from the structure of the netlist (i.e., without needing a functional oracle), together with your confidence and reasoning for each determined bit. Bits you cannot structurally determine should be reported as unknown rather than guessed.
response_format: A single JSON file at submission/recovered_key.json conforming exactly to the schema given in public_spec.interface.
